args.text:
These are the duties for this position at the GS-12. If you're selected at a lower grade level, you'll have the chance to learn all these duties, with training to help you grow in the position.

As a TECHNICAL WRITER-EDITOR, you will:

Handle the contents of documents and Federal Register publications properly so they're published accurately, on time and with legal effect.

Manage the work, whether you're working on your own, in a team or leading others, to publish all documents accurately and on time and achieve all program goals.

Understand and properly address customer needs across every part of the Federal Register publication process, fulfilling the Office of the Federal Register's program responsibilities.

Understand and properly use the technical resources available for and connected with Federal Register publication processes, including information technology, legacy systems and other technical resources.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

This opportunity is also open to Status Candidates under Announcement ST-12632063-25-SW.

Have a look at that announcement for the open period, eligibility and how to apply.

Your experience can come from the public sector, private sector or volunteer service. One year of experience means full-time work; part-time work is counted on a prorated basis. To get full credit for your work experience, please give employment dates as month/day/year and the number of hours you worked each week on your résumé.

A one year probationary period may be required.

You must successfully complete a background investigation.

Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment when the agency asks, to determine your suitability for Federal employment.

If you're a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, certify that you've registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to do so.

Go through a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) process requiring two forms of identification from the Form i-9. Federal law requires all new hires in the U.S. to have their identity and employment eligibility verified.

Please refer to "Conditions of Employment."

Click "Print Preview" to read through the entire announcement before applying.

You must be U.S. Citizens or U.S. Nationals.

Qualifications

You must meet these requirements by this announcement's closing date.

Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position includes:

Editing legal or regulatory documents written by others to make sure they meet style and formatting requirements before being developed for publication; AND

Recognising and analysing production problems and coming up with solutions; AND

Communicating information effectively and diplomatically to internal and/or external audiences to advance program goals.

OR

EDUCATION: A master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related.

OR

COMBINATION OF EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Note: Only graduate study beyond the first year (18 semester hours) qualifies for the GS-9.

NOTE: Undergraduate and Graduate Education: Must have included a total of 15 semester hours in an appropriate scientific, technical, or social science field(s), and at least one course above the introductory level in the field(s) covered by the position. For technical manuals and specifications writers or editors, the equivalent of 15 semester hours may have come through vocational or educational training above high school level at a public, private, or Armed Forces school.

Additional information

We may fill one or more vacancies by selecting from this announcement or any other source.

This announcement may be used to fill similar positions in other organisations within the National Archives and Records Administration.

This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260.

We offer telework opportunities under Agency policy.

We offer alternative and flexible work schedule opportunities under Agency policy.

document_config.guidance: Official prose (terms, policy, minutes, a job ad, an encyclopedia entry): keep every obligation, condition, name and number exact, and quoted documents verbatim. Aussify the connecting prose; no swearing at anyone.
document_config.embellishment_guidance: Dinkum: retell it in a genuine Aussie voice. Rephrase freely so each sentence sounds said, not translated; the odd opener, connective or tag-on where a talker would use one; the original's points in its order. Colour hangs off what's there: no new scenes, asides or punchlines. Where the genre keeps its form exact (a notice, a doc, official prose), the voice goes into everything around what's kept: say the connecting prose the way a local would explain it to a mate, at the level's weight, not in the original's officialese with a word or two swapped. What's kept includes the force of what it says: an obligation, a decision, a finding or a stated aim keeps its verb's weight ("we consider you responsible" isn't "we reckon"; "reaffirmed" isn't "doubled down"; a goal isn't "while they're at it").

result.scope: Issues: flagged phrases, swearing over the cap, US spelling and US words. Warnings: the guide's style rules and swearing density; fidelity to the original (length, names, numbers). Not checked: invented slang.
